source.note: Search summary of third-party listings: 16 runs (30% beginner, 50% intermediate, 20% advanced), 52 km of slopes, '20 lifts and 1 gondola' (Adam gondola) — unclear whether the gondola is within the 20, so the total is left unknown. Attribution between listings approximate

character: The largest single resort in the Hakuba Valley, rising above Happo village with over 1,000 m of vertical and views of the Northern Alps. It hosted alpine events at the 1998 Nagano Olympics and is part of the Hakuba Valley ticket and the Epic Pass's Hakuba Valley allowance.
learning: About 30% of runs are rated beginner (search summary). Reference, confirm: ski schools (including English-language lessons) and rentals operate in Happo village; the upper mountain is steeper.

season.typicalText: Lifts usually start turning in early December, with the full valley open by mid-December; seasons end between late March and early May depending on the resort
season.notes: As of the search, Hakuba 2026-27 opening dates had not been announced. OnTheSnow projects about 4 Dec 2026 for Hakuba Valley (a projection, not an announcement). A 2025-26 opening-dates list gave 1 Dec 2025 for 'Hakuba' without naming the resort. The resort published a separate 2025-26 opening notice (see links).

prices.note: 2025-26 figure; the 2026-27 Happo-One price had not been published when searched (to be added by December 2026).

prices.note: Valid at all ten Hakuba Valley resorts. Child ¥6,400. Valid from each resort's opening day (around December 2026) to its closing day (March to early May 2027).

source.note: Search summary of the official Hakuba Valley lift-ticket page

airports.basis: Estimate from typical routing (Chuo and Nagano expressways to Azumino, then north on Route 147/148); not a routing-service result. Most visitors instead take the Hokuriku Shinkansen to Nagano and a bus.
Estimate from typical routing (via central Tokyo and the Chuo/Nagano expressways); not a routing-service result. Rail via Tokyo and Nagano is the usual alternative.

transfers.name: Hokuriku Shinkansen to Nagano, then express bus to Hakuba
transfers.notes: Usually reached by Hokuriku Shinkansen from Tokyo (or Ueno) to Nagano, about 1.5 h, then by bus. Reference, confirm 2026-27 timetables and fares. The Nagano–Hakuba express bus takes roughly 1–1.25 h.

transfers.name: Direct buses and shared shuttles from Tokyo and the Tokyo airports
transfers.notes: Reference, confirm: seasonal highway buses (e.g. from Shinjuku) and shared airport shuttles run to Hakuba (roughly 4.5–6 h). Operators and fares are not on file.

transfers.name: Hakuba Valley shuttle buses
transfers.notes: Reference, confirm: winter shuttles link Hakuba accommodation areas with the valley's resorts.
